promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Big week, but every single day went over the plan and the hard work piled up fast; next week I am holding volume steady and turning the quality toward marathon pace so you arrive at the race sharp, not fried.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
Short answer: no, and I want to explain why before you talk yourself into it.

You added miles on every single day, including an unplanned Monday run, and your relative effort was almost double your three-week average. That is the fastest way to end up with the same outside-of-knee flare you had three weeks ago, and we cannot afford a lost week with the race on Sun Nov 1.

The 20 mi was a genuine confidence builder and I am glad you got it done with company. But 88% of it sat in zone 3, which is grey-zone running that costs more recovery than it buys fitness. We will do another long run that size, slower, with a marathon-pace finish instead.

The rule for the next six weeks: follow the plan line, do not add distance, and if a session is going well that is the signal it was pitched right, not an invitation to extend it.

new.analysis:
## Why this plan

We are six weeks out and shifting from build into peak, so the quality day moves from threshold reps to marathon-pace work. Your sub-3:45 goal needs about 8:35/mi, and the only way to make that pace feel honest on race day is to spend time at it now, on tired legs, inside a long run.

I am keeping total volume close to last week rather than climbing again, because you already took a big step up and your knee history says we respect that. The long run comes down slightly in distance but gets harder in the back half, which is a better training stimulus than another slow 20.

Easy days are the lever that makes the hard days work. Hold heart rate under 145 on those runs, keep the pace honest, and trust that the quality session and the long run are where the fitness is built. If anything feels off in the knee or elsewhere, email me before the next session rather than pushing through.
